label: <DEL> delimiter step in longer sequences (L>=6)
explanation: Low-end candidate unit that fires almost only at the <DEL> step: 92% of activation mass is there, and it is active on 55% of delimiter steps. Both rate and magnitude rise with sequence length. The share of mass by delimiter t climbs from 0.003 at L=3 to 0.35 at L=9, and to_go=8 has a 46% rate. L>=6 gives the best F1. Inside the delimiter step it also depends weakly on which tokens are in the sequence (first tokens a/b/p/k/o fire a bit more often), but that effect is mild and not captured. Smaller leftovers: the first copy step (recall_idx 1, about 5% of mass) and late original-phase steps in long sequences (about 3%). It is essentially silent at t<3 and on later copy steps. It does not respond to any particular input token apart from <DEL>.
